THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, APRIL 26, 1930

London Derby
Sweepstakes Are
Now Restricted

Government's Views On
Subject Cut Sale
Of Tickets

(Wireless Through Reuter)
London, April 24.—The sweep-
stakes on the Derby this year are
on a much restricted scale as the
result of the declaration recently
made by Mr. J. R. Clynes, the Home
Secretary, setting forth the Govern-
ment's views on the subject.
Mr. Clynes' statement was, in ef-
fect, a warning that sweepstakes
must be conducted privately and
that tickets must not be sold to
the general public.
The Stock Exchange Sweepstake,
which last year reached the enor-
mous total of £1,600,000 owing to
the participation of the public in
all parts of the world, has this year
reached only £7,000 tickets being
sold only to stockbrokers.
The Smithfield meat markets
sweepstake has been abandoned
owing to the threat of proceedings
by the police.

《字林西报》，1930年4月26日，星期六

伦敦德比马赛
彩票抽奖活动
现受限制

政府对此事的观点
遏制了彩票
的销售

（路透社电传）
伦敦，4月24日。——由于内政大臣 J. R. Clynes 先生近日发表声明，阐述了政府在此问题上的立场，今年德比马赛（Derby）的彩票抽奖活动规模已大幅缩减。
Clynes 先生的声明实质上是一项警告，即彩票抽奖活动必须私下进行，且不得向公众出售彩票。
去年因世界各地公众参与而总额高达 1,600,000 英镑的证券交易所彩票抽奖，今年仅售出 7,000 张彩票，且仅向股票经纪人出售。
史密斯菲尔德（Smithfield）肉类市场的彩票抽奖活动已因警方威胁采取法律行动而取消。
